summary: I paired the central prose claims with Tables 1-9, Figures 1-4 and the appendix definitions, using page text and page images where the structured table objects were unsafe. Most headline numbers reconcile: 70/34/36 pilot counts, 97% agreement (33 of 34), 3,187/92/43/29, Table 6 precision counts, Table 8 counts and shares, and Figure 4 county values. I found seven source-fidelity problems. (1) The pilot yield mixes openings with articles. (2) A footnote says both human coders coded the Stord article not relevant, but Table 3 shows a disagreement on exactly that article. (3) The Appendix A.3.2 tie-break rule contradicts its own bysykkelstativ example. (4) Figure 2 colours sykkelmulighet as Leisure although Table 9 gives no Leisure word part for it. (5) The prose says the first quarter of 2024 is missing, while the stated gap is January-April 2024. (6) Figure 2 tick labels 2% and 8% sit at equally spaced positions between 0%, 5% and 10%. (7) Table 2 and Figure 1 leave the reference date for Grettefoss's opening status ambiguous.

findings.finding_summary: Section 3.1.2 states that 'only 2 of the 34 unique articles (about 6 percent)' concern an opening that took place, but the 2 in Figure 1 counts distinct openings, not articles. The same display and Section 3.1.4 show 5 articles coded relevant for those 2 openings.

location.text_quote: Only 2 of the 34 unique articles (about 6 percent) concern an opening that took place.

findings.claim_text: Only 2 of the 34 unique articles (about 6 percent) concern an opening that took place.
findings.evidence_summary: The prose divides a count of openings (2) by a count of articles (34) and calls the result a share of articles. Figure 1 labels one bar 'Distinct openings that took place 2' and another 'Coded “relevant” 5 15 % retained' (articles). Section 3.1.4 states 'Of the five relevant articles, only two unique openings were found' (four Homborsund articles, one Stod). The Figure 1 caption makes the same unit switch with 'Only 2 of 70 search hits'. After the validation recoding there are 3 relevant articles on 2 openings. As worded, 2/34 = 5.9% is the share of unique articles that are distinct openings, not the share concerning an opening that took place. The article-level yield would be 5/34 = 14.7% before recoding, or 3/34 = 8.8% after. The Abstract's 'contained only two actual openings' is correctly worded. The paper does not state which unit the 6 percent is meant to carry. Chart labels were taken from the page-4 text and the page-4 image because the figure_1.png crop omits the chart.

findings.finding_summary: Figure 2's x-axis labels '2%' and '8%' sit on equally spaced gridlines between 0% and 10%, where 5% is the midpoint. The ticks are therefore at equal intervals of 2.5 percentage points, and the labels appear rounded.

findings.evidence_summary: In figure_2.png the tick labels 0%, 2%, 5%, 8% and 10% sit at x of about 507, 654, 801, 948 and 1095 px, i.e. equal spacing of about 147 px, so 5% is the midpoint of 0% and 10%. An evenly spaced axis from 0 to 10 would place ticks at 0, 2.5, 5, 7.5 and 10, so the '2%' and '8%' labels look like rounded values. The bars carry exact value labels, so the plotted values are unaffected, but the axis labels are misleading for reading the scale. The tick spacing was read by eye from the image, so confidence is medium; the paper does not state the tick values.

notes: Parser guidance respected: structured table CSV/markdown objects were not used as primary evidence. Table values were read from page text, with the page-4, 5, 16 and 17 images and figure_2.png and figure_3.png viewed. The table_3.md header was not used because it is merged.

Reconciled without issue: pilot funnel 70 hits - 36 duplicates = 34 unique (49% retained); 5/34 = 14.7% (15%); Table 3/4 agreement (3+30)/34 = 97% and the matching 97% in the Abstract, Introduction and Conclusion; 3,187/92/2/50/43 in Section 5 and Table 6; Table 6 precision counts 19+10+9+5 = 43 and 19+10 = 29; 96 = 92+4 and 44 = 43+1 in footnote 3 (apart from the coder description in SOURCE-002); Table 7 ceremony split 18+26 = 44; Table 8 counts (266,625 + 433,954 = 700,579) and every share; Figure 2 vs Table 8 'bicycle' 9.8%; Figure 4 values vs the prose (Oslo 61, Akershus 52, Telemark 14, Nordland 13, Møre og Romsdal 7, Norway 38); Figure 3 prose 35% to 44% vs Section 6.1.

Not reported as findings: Table 5's 'Length 2,132 m' vs the two road-system ranges (m0-1492 and m0-641 sum to 2,133), which is within plausible rounding of link lengths; the Introduction's 'two independent human coders' wording, since the LLM is benchmarked only against the pilot coder (stated in Section 4); and the prose-only monthly pattern claims in Section 5, for which no display is promised.

Repair: SOURCE-001 numeric check now cites each figure value from a source whose quote contains it; SOURCE-005, SOURCE-006 and SOURCE-007 are source-mapping findings and no longer carry underdetermined numeric checks. Figure 2 tick positions and Figure 3 point positions were re-read from the retained figure crops.
Citation accuracy, causal identification and the econometric specifications in equations (1)-(2) are outside this audit.
